items.title: A quick look at zero-knowledge proofs (14 minute read)
items.content: <article>The idea of a zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) is that there are two parties: the prover and the verifier. The prover asserts that it has a solution to a (generally NP-complete) problem. The prover can convince the verifier of this without sharing the actual solution to the problem. While they are used to secure some cryptocurrencies, that is not their only use case. This article looks at how ZKPs work and how they can be applied to other problems like age verification.</article>

items.title: Why Tiny JPEGs Look Different in Chrome (4 minute read)
items.content: What looks like a rendering bug is actually a clever JPEG decoding optimization in Chrome. Chrome delegates image decoding and rendering to Skia, which does not always decompress the full image and scale it afterward. It computes the closest fraction with a denominator of 8 and decodes the image at that scale, then scales the image further using a more traditional downsampling algorithm until it reaches the desired size. This is why small images can look thicker on some machines.

The Sperm Tracking and Recovery system may bring hope to the 10% of infertile men affected by azoospermia.

items.content: Gemini has reached 1 billion monthly active users (MAU). It is the fastest Google product to have managed that feat. Gemini is now in virtually every Google product and service and is core to Google's flagship search experience. The 1 billion MAU metric only refers to users who have opened the Gemini app or visited the Gemini web interface.

items.title: SpaceXAI Unveils Grok Bot to Work Like a Team of AI Agents (2 minute read)
items.content: SpaceXAI's Grok Bot is designed to act like a team of AI agents capable of handling a wide range of professional work. The agent can sign into various apps and websites, retain information from prior tasks, and share details and context with other agents. SpaceXAI has been using the product internally across its engineering, growth, and marketing teams. It has helped its sales team find new accounts and draft emails and aided its finance team by pulling receipts from emails.

items.title: Apple is working on a way to authenticate that a photo came from an iPhone camera (5 minute read)
items.content: Apple Reference Image is designed to authenticate the source of photos using unique data tied to the iPhone camera hardware that captured them.

items.title: Compute Is Revenue. Revenue Is Collateral (18 minute read)
items.content: Nvidia is attempting to turn a handful of bespoke transactions into a financial production line.

items.content: Cory Solovewicz created an accidental honeypot when he purchased noreply[.]us and noreply[.]net in 2020 and 2024, respectively.

items.title: Following Epic loss, Google has started hosting rival app stores in the Play Store (3 minute read)
items.content: Aptoide, a game-focused store that has been available as a sideloaded client since the early days of Android, is the first third-party app store to arrive in Google Play.

items.title: Everything I Learned Shipping Device Bound Session Credentials (14 minute read)
items.content: Device Bound Session Credentials bind sessions to a private key a browser generates in hardware and cannot export.

items.title: Introducing Muse Glimmer (4 minute read)
items.content: Muse Glimmer is a 30B open weights model optimized for end-to-end agentic task completion, reliable tool use, and multi-step reasoning.

items.title: Nvidia lines up $500 billion in financing as CEO Jensen Huang tells CNBC his chips are ‘investable asset' (4 minute read)
items.content: Nvidia has partnered with six large asset managers on a $500 billion financing push designed to treat compute infrastructure much like commercial real estate, toll roads, or other assets to borrow against. The effort will mobilize third-party capital for hyperscalers, frontier AI labs, and enterprises to build out data centers and acquire Nvidia hardware. It will help Nvidia's customers secure financing without tapping their own balance sheets. Nvidia believes lenders can reliably underwrite compute as a revenue-generating asset with an extended life as its hardware is broadly adopted and transferable across customers.

items.title: See How a Tesla-SpaceX Merger Gives Musk a Shortcut to His $1 Trillion Payday (6 minute read)
items.content: The conditions for Elon Musk to receive his $1 trillion pay package at Tesla could easily be achieved if the company were acquired. There is a clause in the agreement that declares half the targets as good as accomplished if Tesla is acquired or otherwise taken over. This leaves only market-value targets to determine how many shares Musk gets. Musk has considerable say over any offer SpaceX makes for Tesla. Even a stratospheric bid would keep Musk in firm control of the combined company.

items.title: What's the best programming language for coding agents? (57 minute read)
items.content: Anyone who wants to make a strong claim about which language or classes of languages are particularly good with LLMs would need to run quite a few different evaluations. Failures with languages are generally something idiosyncratic, where it's not always obvious how much the issue generalizes across tasks or setups. There's no way to look at the score on one or even several evaluations and draw a conclusion about programming in general. At this point, it would be a mistake to draw a strong conclusion about any particular language.

items.title: No, local models will not win (7 minute read)
items.content: Local models are never going to be as powerful as datacenter models. All of the current frontier models are far too big to run on anything but a full GPU cluster. Smaller models are getting more intelligent, but datacenter models will always be the strongest available. When given a choice, people are going to pick the strongest available model in their price range, the one that frustrates them least, which is always going to be the bigger, more powerful one.

items.title: Learning more about Claude's mathematical capabilities (7 minute read)
items.content: Claude was recently challenged with one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics: the Riemann hypothesis. While Claude didn't succeed, it unexpectedly made strides on a related problem. It improved on a longstanding lower bound for the fraction of zeros of the Riemann zeta function that satisfy the Riemann hypothesis. The result shows that AI models like Claude can extend the impact and reach of mathematicians' ideas in new and sometimes surprising ways.

items.title: Dyna-2 Proves Scaling Laws for Robotics: 1 Million Hours of Human Video Unlocks Zero-Shot Dexterity (4 minute read)
items.content: Dyna-2 is a world-action model (WAM) pre-trained on over one million hours of human video data. Its existence proves that scaling human video data predictably improves zero-shot performance on unseen robot hardware. Dyna-2 achieved an 87% pass rate in real-world zero-shot deployments at customer sites, vastly outperforming the 46% pass rate of its VLA predecessor, Dyna-1. The model uses a new one-step video generation distillation pipeline that drops inference latency by two orders of magnitude for downstream planning.

items.title: Google's classic Search button is gone in a new AI-first homepage (3 minute read)
items.content: Google is testing a version of its homepage where the search button is replaced with an AI Mode button. The new interface allows users to ask about files and use the Brainstorm function without having to log in. Logged-in users are also able to generate images. Ask about files allows users to attach a file before submitting a question, and Brainstorm helps users explore ideas.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Lays Out New AI Vision in 6,500-Word Essay (6 minute read)
items.content: Mark Zuckerberg recently released a wide-ranging essay that outlined a new course of action to spread the wealth and opportunity from AI to users around the world, and to residents of the communities that host the data centers powering it. Zuckerberg's plans include releasing more open-weight models and establishing a $1 billion fund to invest in the communities where Meta hosts data centers. He believes that Meta's approach to developing powerful AI and distributing it as widely as possible is the least likely path to disastrous outcomes for humanity. The commitment marks a significant development in the debate around whether advanced AI is too dangerous to create on an open-source basis.

items.title: ChatGPT starts blocking direct requests to copy an author's style (4 minute read)
items.content: ChatGPT will now instead offer a response that draws on the broad qualities of those authors while remaining distinct in its own voice.

items.title: How I Rebuilt My Development Workstation for Agentic Work (13 minute read)
items.content: This post describes a workstation that is terminal-native, agentic-first, and built around composable tools.

items.title: Interviewing Engineers in the AI Era: Lessons from a Year of Rebuilding (13 minute read)
items.content: Coinbase has rebuilt its engineering interview loop to test how candidates direct AI, evaluate its output, and apply judgment where models fall short.

items.title: Why you might want to build your WebApp in Canvas instead of HTML (7 minute read)
items.content: Canvas is a low-level rendering tool that gives users more control than HTML.

items.title: Revision Prompting improves industrial LLM processes (4 minute read)
items.content: Revision Prompting supplies LLMs with the original input, the original output, and the changes to the input, and instructs it to produce a patch that updates the original output accordingly.

items.title: Amazon cracks down on 'CPU waste' among engineers as agentic AI crunch intensifies (5 minute read)
items.content: AWS is cracking down on internal use of EC2 instances among its engineers. Engineers have been told to reduce CPU waste to ensure the company has enough CPU capacity to meet customer demand. The increased demand for CPU is due to the rise of AI agentic workloads. Other cloud companies are also seeing high demand for CPUs.

items.title: Changing Devtools Is Cheap. Owning Them Isn't (8 minute read)
items.content: The future of software will be powered by high-quality, well-documented building blocks that users can build specialized artifacts on top of. Agents are good at composing high-quality components. Maintainers can provide these components alongside a focus application, and users can choose how to modify their experiences themselves. This allows software to be personalized while still being developed by maintainers that care.

items.title: Google's Westinghouse Bet (9 minute read)
items.content: Google's recent reshuffling of its AI operations has many thinking that the company has failed in the AI race. However, the company may just be refocusing its resources on its strengths. Google Cloud may be a much larger economic opportunity than pursuing its rivals in the frontier AI race. The company's enormous distribution advantage means it doesn't have to compete in the expensive and unprofitable frontier race.

items.title: Agentic Code Quality (11 minute read)
items.content: Software quality now depends on the constraints set around the agents that wrote it. Constraints define what a system is allowed to do. Setting and maintaining these constraints allows developers to build loops that reliably deliver high-quality production software. Agents can propose anything - constraints decide whether a proposal is safe enough, correct, scoped, and useful.

items.title: The first self-driving vehicle on Mars has proven to be a smashing success (4 minute read)
items.content: NASA's Perseverance Mars rover will set a record for the most distance driven by any vehicle on another world sometime next week. The rover's auto navigation system has enabled about 90% of the distance driven by the vehicle to be autonomous. Not having to wait for navigation commands from drivers on Earth has allowed the rover to maximize the amount of scientific return. The vehicle will likely be able to keep driving itself across Mars for many years to come.

items.title: China-Free Batteries Made From Salt Are Finally Here (8 minute read)
items.content: Peak Energy, a US-based startup, has raised tens of millions of dollars to build a factory for its sodium-ion battery packs. It already has more than $1.1 billion in announced deals with customers. Sodium batteries have less-intensive cooling needs than lithium-ion packs, and they are less likely to catch fire. Another US-based startup, Inlyte Energy, is working on another type of sodium-based battery that can't catch fire at all.

items.title: Apple Explores Shaking Up Its Smartwatch for a New Era (13 minute read)
items.content: The Apple Watch continues to attract new buyers and remains the top-selling smartwatch. However, the company's industrial design team has been exploring a broad rethink of Apple's smartwatches and is evaluating several different directions. Apple needs to adapt to the rise of screenless fitness bands and smart rings, which are cheaper, lighter, and more fun and convenient to use for many people. The company aims to inject new life into its Wearables, Home, and Accessories segment, which has struggled to generate meaningful growth in recent years.

items.title: Now we have a timeline of the OpenAI accidental attack against Hugging Face (6 minute read)
items.content: OpenAI recently gave a presentation about the Hugging Face incident. The talk is short and information dense and provides full details of what happened and how things played out inside OpenAI. This post presents the timeline of events and details how the hack occurred. A video of the presentation is available in the post.
